description: PostgreSQL 18 geometric arrays, lower bounds, catalogs, and canonical transport parity
sql: SELECT ARRAY['(1,2)','(3,4)']::point[] AS points, ARRAY['{1,2,3}','{4,5,6}']::line[] AS lines, ARRAY['[(1,2),(3,4)]','[(5,6),(7,8)]']::lseg[] AS segments;
SELECT '[0:1]={"(1,2)","(3,4)"}'::point[] AS bounded_points, array_dims('[0:1]={"(1,2)","(3,4)"}'::point[]) AS point_dims, ('[0:1]={"(1,2)","(3,4)"}'::point[])[0] AS first_point;
CREATE TABLE type_matrix_geometric_transport (id int4 PRIMARY KEY, points point[], lines line[], segments lseg[], boxes box[], paths path[], polygons polygon[], circles circle[]);
SELECT points, lines, segments, boxes, paths, polygons, circles FROM type_matrix_geometric_transport WHERE id = 1;
SELECT oid, typname::text, typelem, typarray, typdelim::text FROM pg_type WHERE oid IN (600, 601, 602, 603, 604, 628, 629, 718, 719, 1017, 1018, 1019, 1020, 1027) ORDER BY oid;
SELECT format_type(1017, -1), format_type(1018, -1), format_type(1019, -1), format_type(1020, -1), format_type(1027, -1), format_type(629, -1), format_type(719, -1);
